notes: Spent about six turns clicking for credits up to 39 with no breakers and no plan, and only Spreed into unrezzed ice. Never ran the naked Server 3 Sting! or the advancing remotes, so the Corp scored 7 points out of servers it could have contested.

Sat on 16-24 credits for several turns clicking for credits and drawing into discards, and tagged the Runner with Oppo Research without ever punishing it. Tomorrow's Headline went behind a Tsarevna the Runner had already shown it would take damage to get through, and was stolen; the flatline came from Tsarevna damage rather than from a plan.

Ran the unchanged top of open R&D three or four times a turn (hitting Behold! repeatedly), then ran HQ through Virtual Service Agent over and over at 0 credits, piling up tags and declining every agenda it could not afford. Facechecked Tsarevna with a tiny grip and walked into a foreseeable End of the Line flatline against NBN.

Scored steadily out of Server 1, but spent many clicks putting ice on a string of empty new remotes and advancing ice. It sat on 15-27 credits while the Runner did nothing, so the win came far later than it should have.

Sensible R&D and HQ pressure with Trick Shot and Gauss, cashed in breakers for Degree Mill at the right moment, and took a winning facecheck at 6 points. Only minor inefficiencies, such as a stray credit click and installing a second Self-modifying Code.

Never installed an agenda: it clicked for credits up to 21 and discarded every turn while HQ filled with agendas behind a single Ping. The Runner stole Bellona, Tomorrow's Headline and two False Leads straight from HQ.

Good early HQ and Archives pressure got it to 6 points, then it stalled for 15 turns running empty Archives twice a turn and clicking for credits to 37 with an empty grip. It never drew up to pressure HQ, R&D or the remote while the Corp passed every turn.

Clicked for credits to 22 for three turns while the Corp installed and scored two Regenesis from remotes it could have contested. After Data Loop emptied its grip it kept running R&D against Personal Evolution and flatlined on stealing an agenda, which was foreseeable.

Twenty turns without installing an agenda: it clicked for credits and discarded, and later spent two clicks a turn trashing resources. Bellona, Degree Mill and False Lead were stolen from an HQ protected only by Ping.
A clean fast-advance plan: scored Send a Message and two SDS out of an iced remote, using NGO Front and Government Subsidy for economy. A few idle credit clicks while already rich.

Ran a coherent AU Co./Bladderwort net-damage plan, but scored both False Leads out of naked remotes and stayed on 0-3 credits all game. It only got away with this because the Runner ignored remotes entirely.

Kept running while tagged against NBN and took an End of the Line hit that cost four cards, facechecked Ping on R&D, and wasted two Pinhole Threadings on Archives. Recovered well and finished with a strong Cupellation multi-access on HQ.

Answered sabotage by trashing agendas from HQ into an unprotected Archives, giving away 6 points in one run, and never iced R&D or Archives. It burned 7 credits on Oppo Research tags with no follow-up and spent the rest of the game clicking for credits.

Twice ran a naked Bellona three times in a row while unable to pay 5 to steal it, when one credit click first would have made the steal; the Corp scored both. Repeated runs on the same R&D top card and ignored the final naked remote that won the game.

Facechecked Pharos and Akhet early, then clicked for credits to 26 for most of the game while the Corp scored three agendas from one remote. It also pointed Boomerang at the wrong Akhet and never pressed the server even while the Corp was on 0-3 credits.

No ice for two turns while clicking for credits, and it answered sabotage by trashing agendas into an open Archives, which was stolen at once. It also played IP Enforcement to no effect; the game was lost by turn 3.

Facechecked Hortum, Tree Line and Akhet early, then sat on 20-45 credits for ten turns clicking for credits and running empty Archives. It never contested the remote the Corp scored from, including the final Above the Law installed and advanced right in front of it.

Spent turns 3-8 clicking for credits to 25 and discarding before doing anything, but then scored a stream of small agendas from iced remotes, with Snare! as a good trap. It won but was very slow to start.

A coherent AU Co. damage plan: Semak-samun held the scoring remote and two Bladderworts ground the Runner out for a flatline. It lost a False Lead through Anemone and ran on 0-3 credits throughout, but this suited the deck.

Won by hammering an unprotected R&D, but repeatedly ran the same unchanged top card and sat on 0 credits for four turns. It let the Corp score Tomorrow's Headline from a naked remote it never checked.
